examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula for Cosine
examples.worked_solution:
We can use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\cos^2\theta -\sin^2\theta=\cos 2\theta.
$$

Letting $\theta = 3x$ gives

$$
\cos^2 3x - \sin^2 3x = \cos 6x,
$$

and therefore,

$$
\eqalign{
		{\int} \left(\cos^2 3x - \sin^2 3x\right ) \, \textrm{d}x&=\int  \cos 6x\, \textrm{d}x\
								&=\dfrac{1}{6}\sin6x+ C.\
                                                                
	}
$$

Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{4}),$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\pi ,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{\pi }5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{4})\,\text{d}x.
$$

In this case, we use the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta 
$$

Letting $\theta =\frac{x}{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2}) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+5\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
